review.source: Actual written N1904 and the publisher rows, reviewed against the displayed BSB by Claude (Anthropic); independent peer review recorded in the registry.

14:1.sourceText: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν Ἰκονίῳ κατὰ τὸ αὐτὸ εἰσελθεῖν αὐτοὺς εἰς τὴν συναγωγὴν τῶν Ἰουδαίων καὶ λαλῆσαι οὕτως ὥστε πιστεῦσαι Ἰουδαίων τε καὶ Ἑλλήνων πολὺ πλῆθος.
14:1.targetText: At Iconium, Paul and Barnabas went as usual into the Jewish synagogue, where they spoke so well that a great number of Jews and Greeks believed.

groups.note: κατὰ τὸ αὐτό ("in the same way") is rendered as usual.
BSB names Paul and Barnabas for the pronoun αὐτούς ("they").
BSB joins the second infinitive clause with where for καί ("and").

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the narrative formula Ἐγένετο δέ ("and it came about") untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
In τε … καί ("both … and") English renders only καί.

14:2.sourceText: οἱ δὲ ἀπειθήσαντες Ἰουδαῖοι ἐπήγειραν καὶ ἐκάκωσαν τὰς ψυχὰς τῶν ἐθνῶν κατὰ τῶν ἀδελφῶν.
14:2.targetText: But the unbelieving Jews stirred up the Gentiles and poisoned their minds against the brothers.

14:3.sourceText: ἱκανὸν μὲν οὖν χρόνον διέτριψαν παρρησιαζόμενοι ἐπὶ τῷ Κυρίῳ τῷ μαρτυροῦντι ἐπὶ τῷ λόγῳ τῆς χάριτος αὐτοῦ, διδόντι σημεῖα καὶ τέρατα γίνεσθαι διὰ τῶν χειρῶν αὐτῶν.
14:3.targetText: So Paul and Barnabas spent considerable time there, speaking boldly for the Lord, who affirmed the message of His grace by enabling them to perform signs and wonders.

groups.note: The article with the participle, "the one bearing witness", is rendered who affirmed.
The pronoun αὐτῶν ("their" hands) becomes the object of enabling.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB renders μὲν οὖν with So alone; μέν has no separate counterpart.
BSB renders μαρτυροῦντι ἐπί ("bearing witness to") with the transitive verb affirmed.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB renders διὰ τῶν χειρῶν αὐτῶν ("through their hands") as enabling them to perform, without a word for the hands.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subjects; the Greek gives them only in the verb ending.
English adds the place; the Greek has no word for there.

14:4.sourceText: ἐσχίσθη δὲ τὸ πλῆθος τῆς πόλεως, καὶ οἱ μὲν ἦσαν σὺν τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις, οἱ δὲ σὺν τοῖς ἀποστόλοις.
14:4.targetText: The people of the city were divided. Some sided with the Jews, and others with the apostles.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective δέ untranslated.
BSB starts a new sentence and leaves καί untranslated.
The μέν … δέ contrast is carried by Some … others.

14:5.sourceText: ὡς δὲ ἐγένετο ὁρμὴ τῶν ἐθνῶν τε καὶ Ἰουδαίων σὺν τοῖς ἄρχουσιν αὐτῶν ὑβρίσαι καὶ λιθοβολῆσαι αὐτούς,
14:5.targetText: But when the Gentiles and Jews, together with their rulers, set out to mistreat and stone them,

groups.note: ἐγένετο ὁρμή ("an attempt arose") is rendered set out.

unmappedSource.reason: In τε … καί ("both … and") English renders only καί.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

14:6.sourceText: συνιδόντες κατέφυγον εἰς τὰς πόλεις τῆς Λυκαονίας Λύστραν καὶ Δέρβην καὶ τὴν περίχωρον·
14:6.targetText: they found out about it and fled to the Lycaonian cities of Lystra and Derbe and to the surrounding region,

groups.note: The one εἰς governs both the cities and the surrounding region; BSB repeats to.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies an object; the participle συνιδόντες has none.
English joins found out, rendering the participle συνιδόντες, to the main verb fled.

14:7.targetText: where they continued to preach the gospel.

14:8.sourceText: Καί τις ἀνὴρ ἀδύνατος ἐν Λύστροις τοῖς ποσὶν ἐκάθητο, χωλὸς ἐκ κοιλίας μητρὸς αὐτοῦ ὃς οὐδέποτε περιεπάτησεν.
14:8.targetText: In Lystra there sat a man crippled in his feet, who was lame from birth and had never walked.

groups.note: κοιλίας μητρὸς αὐτοῦ ("his mother's womb") is rendered birth, as in Acts 3:2.
BSB places the relative ὅς ("who") before lame, so that it introduces both predicates.

unmappedSource.reason: The opening καί only links to the previous verse and is not separately expressed.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the copula; the Greek has none.
English joins the two predicates; the Greek has no conjunction here.

14:9.sourceText: οὗτος ἤκουεν τοῦ Παύλου λαλοῦντος· ὃς ἀτενίσας αὐτῷ καὶ ἰδὼν ὅτι ἔχει πίστιν τοῦ σωθῆναι,
14:9.targetText: This man was listening to the words of Paul, who looked intently at him and saw that he had faith to be healed.

groups.note: BSB's Greek text has a different form of this verb; the English renders the same verb.
The article with the infinitive, τοῦ σωθῆναι, is rendered to be healed.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

14:10.sourceText: εἶπεν μεγάλῃ φωνῇ Ἀνάστηθι ἐπὶ τοὺς πόδας σου ὀρθός. καὶ ἥλατο καὶ περιεπάτει.
14:10.targetText: In a loud voice Paul called out, “Stand up on your feet!” And the man jumped up and began to walk.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the speaker; the Greek gives him only in the verb ending.
English names the subject; the Greek gives him only in the verb ending.

14:11.sourceText: οἵ τε ὄχλοι ἰδόντες ὃ ἐποίησεν Παῦλος ἐπῆραν τὴν φωνὴν αὐτῶν Λυκαονιστὶ λέγοντες Οἱ θεοὶ ὁμοιωθέντες ἀνθρώποις κατέβησαν πρὸς ἡμᾶς,
14:11.targetText: When the crowds saw what Paul had done, they lifted up their voices in the Lycaonian language: “The gods have come down to us in human form!”

groups.note: The adverb Λυκαονιστί ("in Lycaonian") is rendered in the Lycaonian language.
ὁμοιωθέντες ("made like") is rendered in … form.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective τε untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB introduces the quotation with a colon and leaves λέγοντες ("saying") untranslated.

14:12.sourceText: ἐκάλουν τε τὸν Βαρνάβαν Δία, τὸν δὲ Παῦλον Ἑρμῆν, ἐπειδὴ αὐτὸς ἦν ὁ ἡγούμενος τοῦ λόγου.
14:12.targetText: Barnabas they called Zeus, and Paul they called Hermes, because he was the chief speaker.

groups.note: The one verb ἐκάλουν governs both names; BSB repeats they called.
The article with the participle, ὁ ἡγούμενος ("the one leading"), is rendered the chief.
ἡγούμενος τοῦ λόγου ("leading the speech") is rendered chief speaker.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective τε untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

14:13.sourceText: ὅ τε ἱερεὺς τοῦ Διὸς τοῦ ὄντος πρὸ τῆς πόλεως, ταύρους καὶ στέμματα ἐπὶ τοὺς πυλῶνας ἐνέγκας, σὺν τοῖς ὄχλοις ἤθελεν θύειν.
14:13.targetText: The priest of Zeus, whose temple was just outside the city, brought bulls and wreaths to the city gates, hoping to offer a sacrifice along with the crowds.

groups.note: The article with the participle, τοῦ ὄντος ("the one being"), is rendered whose … was.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective τε untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the temple; the Greek speaks of Zeus himself as before the city.
English specifies whose gates; πυλῶνας means only gateways.

14:14.sourceText: ἀκούσαντες δὲ οἱ ἀπόστολοι Βαρνάβας καὶ Παῦλος, διαρρήξαντες τὰ ἱμάτια ἑαυτῶν ἐξεπήδησαν εἰς τὸν ὄχλον, κράζοντες
14:14.targetText: But when the apostles Barnabas and Paul found out about this, they tore their clothes and rushed into the crowd, shouting,

groups.note: BSB's Greek text has a different form of this pronoun here, with the same meaning.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies an object; the participle ἀκούσαντες has none.
English joins tore, rendering the participle διαρρήξαντες, to the main verb rushed.

14:15.sourceText: καὶ λέγοντες Ἄνδρες, τί ταῦτα ποιεῖτε; καὶ ἡμεῖς ὁμοιοπαθεῖς ἐσμεν ὑμῖν ἄνθρωποι, εὐαγγελιζόμενοι ὑμᾶς ἀπὸ τούτων τῶν ματαίων ἐπιστρέφειν ἐπὶ θεὸν ζῶντα, ὃς ἐποίησεν τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ τὴν γῆν καὶ τὴν θάλασσαν καὶ πάντα τὰ ἐν αὐτοῖς·
14:15.targetText: “Men, why are you doing this? We too are only men, human like you. We are bringing you good news that you should turn from these worthless things to the living God, who made heaven and earth and sea and everything in them.

groups.note: ὁμοιοπαθεῖς ("of like nature") is rendered human like.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB lets shouting (14:14) introduce the speech and leaves καὶ λέγοντες ("and saying") untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds only for emphasis; the Greek has no word for it.

14:16.sourceText: ὃς ἐν ταῖς παρῳχημέναις γενεαῖς εἴασεν πάντα τὰ ἔθνη πορεύεσθαι ταῖς ὁδοῖς αὐτῶν·
14:16.targetText: In past generations, He let all nations go their own way.

groups.note: The relative ὅς ("who") is rendered He, as BSB starts a new sentence.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

14:17.sourceText: καίτοι οὐκ ἀμάρτυρον αὑτὸν ἀφῆκεν ἀγαθουργῶν, οὐρανόθεν ὑμῖν ὑετοὺς διδοὺς καὶ καιροὺς καρποφόρους, ἐμπιπλῶν τροφῆς καὶ εὐφροσύνης τὰς καρδίας ὑμῶν.
14:17.targetText: Yet He has not left Himself without testimony to His goodness: He gives you rain from heaven and fruitful seasons, filling your hearts with food and gladness.”

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

14:18.sourceText: καὶ ταῦτα λέγοντες μόλις κατέπαυσαν τοὺς ὄχλους τοῦ μὴ θύειν αὐτοῖς.
14:18.targetText: Even with these words, Paul and Barnabas could hardly stop the crowds from sacrificing to them.

groups.note: The participle λέγοντες ("saying") is rendered with … words.
τοῦ μή with the infinitive after a verb of restraining is rendered from.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subjects; the Greek gives them only in the verb ending.

14:19.sourceText: Ἐπῆλθαν δὲ ἀπὸ Ἀντιοχείας καὶ Ἰκονίου Ἰουδαῖοι, καὶ πείσαντες τοὺς ὄχλους καὶ λιθάσαντες τὸν Παῦλον ἔσυρον ἔξω τῆς πόλεως, νομίζοντες αὐτὸν τεθνηκέναι.
14:19.targetText: Then some Jews arrived from Antioch and Iconium and won over the crowds. They stoned Paul and dragged him outside the city, presuming he was dead.

groups.note: BSB starts a new sentence at They stoned and places this καί before dragged.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the object of dragged; the Greek has none.

14:20.sourceText: κυκλωσάντων δὲ τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτὸν ἀναστὰς εἰσῆλθεν εἰς τὴν πόλιν. Καὶ τῇ ἐπαύριον ἐξῆλθεν σὺν τῷ Βαρνάβᾳ εἰς Δέρβην.
14:20.targetText: But after the disciples had gathered around him, he got up and went back into the city. And the next day he left with Barnabas for Derbe.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins got up, rendering the participle ἀναστάς, to the main verb went.
English adds back; εἰσῆλθεν means only "entered".

14:21.sourceText: εὐαγγελιζόμενοί τε τὴν πόλιν ἐκείνην καὶ μαθητεύσαντες ἱκανοὺς ὑπέστρεψαν εἰς τὴν Λύστραν καὶ εἰς Ἰκόνιον καὶ εἰς Ἀντιόχειαν,
14:21.targetText: They preached the gospel to that city and made many disciples. Then they returned to Lystra, Iconium, and Antioch,

groups.note: BSB's Greek text has a different form of this verb; the English renders the same verb.

unmappedSource.reason: In τε … καί ("both … and") English renders only καί.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The first καί of the list is rendered by a comma.
BSB does not repeat the preposition εἰς ("to") before Iconium and Antioch.

unmappedTarget.reason: English starts a new sentence with Then; the Greek has no connective before the main verb.

14:22.sourceText: ἐπιστηρίζοντες τὰς ψυχὰς τῶν μαθητῶν, παρακαλοῦντες ἐμμένειν τῇ πίστει, καὶ ὅτι διὰ πολλῶν θλίψεων δεῖ ἡμᾶς εἰσελθεῖν εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ Θεοῦ.
14:22.targetText: strengthening the souls of the disciples and encouraging them to continue in the faith. “We must endure many hardships to enter the kingdom of God,” they said.

groups.note: διά ("through") many hardships is rendered endure many hardships.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB makes the ὅτι clause a separate quotation, so the καί joining it to continue in the faith has no English word.
BSB turns the ὅτι clause into a direct quotation, so ὅτι ("that") has no English word.
εἰς ("into") is absorbed into enter.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the object of encouraging; the Greek has none.
English supplies a speech verb for the quotation; the Greek clause depends on encouraging.
English joins the participles strengthening and encouraging, which the Greek sets side by side without a conjunction.

14:23.sourceText: χειροτονήσαντες δὲ αὐτοῖς κατ’ ἐκκλησίαν πρεσβυτέρους, προσευξάμενοι μετὰ νηστειῶν παρέθεντο αὐτοὺς τῷ Κυρίῳ εἰς ὃν πεπιστεύκεισαν.
14:23.targetText: Paul and Barnabas appointed elders for them in each church, praying and fasting as they entrusted them to the Lord, in whom they had believed.

groups.note: μετά ("with") fasting is rendered and fasting.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective δέ untranslated.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subjects; the Greek gives them only in the participle.
English links the participles to the main verb with as; the Greek has no word for it.

14:24.sourceText: καὶ διελθόντες τὴν Πισιδίαν ἦλθον εἰς τὴν Παμφυλίαν,
14:24.targetText: After passing through Pisidia, they came to Pamphylia.

unmappedSource.reason: The opening καί only links to the previous verse and is not separately expressed.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

14:25.sourceText: καὶ λαλήσαντες ἐν Πέργῃ τὸν λόγον κατέβησαν εἰς Ἀτταλίαν,
14:25.targetText: And when they had spoken the word in Perga, they went down to Attalia.

groups.note: Same name, spelled differently in BSB's Greek text.

14:26.sourceText: κἀκεῖθεν ἀπέπλευσαν εἰς Ἀντιόχειαν, ὅθεν ἦσαν παραδεδομένοι τῇ χάριτι τοῦ Θεοῦ εἰς τὸ ἔργον ὃ ἐπλήρωσαν.
14:26.targetText: From Attalia they sailed to Antioch, where they had been commended to the grace of God for the work they had just completed.

groups.note: κἀκεῖθεν ("and from there") is rendered From Attalia.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
English leaves the relative ὅ ("which") unexpressed.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds just; the Greek has no word for it.

14:27.sourceText: Παραγενόμενοι δὲ καὶ συναγαγόντες τὴν ἐκκλησίαν, ἀνήγγελλον ὅσα ἐποίησεν ὁ Θεὸς μετ’ αὐτῶν, καὶ ὅτι ἤνοιξεν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν θύραν πίστεως.
14:27.targetText: When they arrived, they gathered the church together and reported all that God had done through them, and how He had opened the door of faith to the Gentiles.

groups.note: BSB makes the second participle a main verb and places this καί before reported.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective δέ untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

14:28.sourceText: διέτριβον δὲ χρόνον οὐκ ὀλίγον σὺν τοῖς μαθηταῖς.
14:28.targetText: And they spent a long time there with the disciples.

groups.note: οὐκ ὀλίγον ("not a little") is rendered a long.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds the place; the Greek has no word for there.
